text: There was one night while training and debugging a model pipeline for me.
Four terminals open, Databricks logs scrolling endlessly, coffee cold for an hour,
when our voice cut through the noise without warning.
Not the serious conversation, not the emotional moment, just the way she laughed,
after interrupting herself mid-sentence, days earlier.
And suddenly the entire debugging session disappeared behind that one tiny memory.
That's the unsettling thing about attachment.
The brain doesn't archive what matters logically.
The microscopic human details you never consciously choose to keep.
The point's real subject arrives near the end.
